meta.title: Free Resources for Developers and Vibe Coders, Part 2: AI, Design, Dev Tools and Hosting
meta.description: Free AI models, APIs and coding tools, UI and design assets, developer utilities, hosting, automation and launch tools, with free-tier limits and commercial-use warnings where verified.
meta.generated_by: Claude (Anthropic): web research, GitHub API checks and npm registry checks run on the generated_on date

part_of_set.note: Resource ids are unique across files 1 and 2. Collections may reference ids in either file (see items[].file). Merge the two resources arrays to get the full database.

field_definitions.id: Stable unique slug across both resource files.
field_definitions.name: Display name.
field_definitions.repo_url: GitHub repo if one exists and was verified, else null.
field_definitions.category / subcategory: Ids that map to the categories array.
field_definitions.is_100_percent_free: True only for fully_free and open_source entries. Use this for a strict '100 percent free' filter.
field_definitions.popularity / hidden_gem: hidden_gem is true when popularity is niche.
field_definitions.license: SPDX id or descriptive text when known, else null.
field_definitions.free_tier: For free_tier entries: summary of limits, the date it was verified (null if not verified this session) and the source.
field_definitions.github: Repo facts read from the GitHub API on checked_on: stars, license_spdx, archived, last_push, maintenance_status.
field_definitions.verification: How and when the entry was checked (see enums.verification_level).

pricing_type.fully_free: Free to use with no paid tier for the core resource.
pricing_type.open_source: Source code is public; free to use and self-host (hosting or hosted plans may cost money).
pricing_type.free_tier: A permanent free plan exists but with limits; paid plans also exist. NOT 100 percent free.
pricing_type.free_for_students: Free only for verified students or similar groups.

commercial_use.yes: Permissive license or explicit terms allowing commercial use.
commercial_use.yes_with_conditions: Allowed with conditions such as attribution, copyleft or usage limits; read the license.
commercial_use.no: Free plan or license does not allow commercial use (verified).
commercial_use.check_terms: Unclear or varies; read the terms before commercial use.
commercial_use.not_applicable: Learning/reading resource; no reuse license involved.

verification_level.verified_via_github_api: Repo, license, stars, last push and archived flag read from the GitHub API on the check date.
verification_level.repo_verified_website_not_checked: Linked GitHub repo verified via API; the website URL was not fetched.
verification_level.verified_via_web_search: Existence and key facts confirmed in web search results on the check date; see sources[].
verification_level.established_knowledge_recheck_advised: Long-running, widely referenced resource included from prior knowledge; URL not fetched. Run a link check before publishing.

meta.how_free_is_free: Many AI and hosting products have a free tier rather than being fully free. Use is_100_percent_free for strict filtering and show pricing_type plus free_tier.summary for everything else.
known_limitations: This is a curated, verified subset, not the whole internet. It is designed to be extended with the same schema.
Reddit and social platforms were not scraped; subreddit entries were chosen from web-search discovery plus prior knowledge.
Free-tier numbers change frequently. Only entries whose free_tier.verified_on is set were checked on the generated_on date, and several of those rely on third-party trackers rather than vendor pages.
Entries marked established_knowledge_recheck_advised were not fetched in this session. Run a link check before publishing.
meta.legal_notice: This is an independent, curated index of third-party resources. Names, logos and trademarks belong to their owners and no endorsement is implied. Descriptions are original text. Always follow each resource's own license and terms.

resources.name: Hugging Face Hub
resources.description: The central hub for open AI: millions of downloadable models, hundreds of thousands of datasets and over a million Spaces (demo apps). Browsing and downloading is free; compute is metered separately.

free_tier.summary: Free account: download public models/datasets, host public Spaces on free shared CPU hardware, a small daily ZeroGPU allowance (about 5 minutes/day reported) and about $0.10/month of Inference Provider credits. PRO is $9/month.

resources.notes: Each model has its own license; read the model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Hugging Face Spaces
resources.description: Directory of community-built AI demo apps you can try in the browser and duplicate for your own use (Gradio, Streamlit, Docker). Great for discovering free tools such as background removal, TTS, image generation and OCR.

free_tier.summary: Free shared CPU Spaces; GPU access via ZeroGPU has a small daily quota on free accounts.

resources.name: Hugging Face Datasets
resources.description: Searchable hub of open datasets for text, images, audio and more, loadable with one line of code. Each dataset has its own license.

resources.name: Hugging Face Daily Papers
resources.description: Community-curated feed of trending AI research papers with links to models and code.

resources.name: arXiv
resources.description: Open-access preprint server where most AI and computer-science research appears first.

resources.name: Ollama Model Library
resources.description: Catalogue of open-weight models packaged so you can run them locally with a single Ollama command.

resources.name: Qwen (Alibaba) on Hugging Face
resources.description: Alibaba's Qwen open-weight models: general chat, coding, vision and embedding variants in many sizes. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Mistral AI on Hugging Face
resources.description: Open-weight models from Mistral AI, several released under the permissive Apache-2.0 license. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: DeepSeek on Hugging Face
resources.description: Open-weight reasoning and coding models from DeepSeek. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Google (Gemma) on Hugging Face
resources.description: Google's open-weight Gemma models (small, laptop-friendly LLMs and multimodal variants) under Google's Gemma terms of use. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Meta Llama on Hugging Face
resources.description: Meta's Llama open-weight models, released under the custom Llama community license (not an OSI open-source license); access may require accepting terms.

resources.name: OpenAI open-weight models on Hugging Face
resources.description: OpenAI's open-weight releases such as the gpt-oss models and Whisper speech recognition; check each model card for license and hardware needs.

resources.name: Microsoft Phi on Hugging Face
resources.description: Microsoft's small language models (Phi family) designed to run on modest hardware, plus other research models. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: SmolLM (Hugging Face TB)
resources.description: Small, fully open language models from Hugging Face designed for on-device use and learning. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Allen AI (OLMo)
resources.description: The Allen Institute for AI publishes OLMo language models with open training data and code, useful for research and study. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Black Forest Labs (FLUX)
resources.description: Image-generation models such as FLUX. Some variants permit commercial use while others are non-commercial, so check each license.

resources.name: NVIDIA on Hugging Face
resources.description: NVIDIA's open models and datasets (language, speech, vision), often under NVIDIA's own open-model license. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Moonshot AI (Kimi) on Hugging Face
resources.description: Open-weight Kimi models focused on long-context and agentic use. Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: Z.ai (GLM) on Hugging Face
resources.description: Open-weight GLM language and vision models from Z.ai (Zhipu). Open-weight model family; licenses differ per model (some permissive, some custom), so read each model card before commercial use.

resources.name: LMArena
resources.description: Crowd-sourced arena where you chat with two anonymous models and vote; maintains public leaderboards including for coding and web-dev tasks.

resources.name: Artificial Analysis
resources.description: Independent comparisons of AI models and API providers on quality, speed and price. Handy before choosing a paid or free API.

resources.name: OpenRouter Rankings
resources.description: Usage-based rankings showing which models developers actually route traffic to, useful as a reality check next to benchmark scores.

resources.name: Ollama
resources.description: Simplest way to download and run open-weight LLMs locally with a CLI and a local API that many tools can talk to.

resources.name: llama.cpp
resources.description: Efficient C/C++ inference engine for running quantised LLMs on CPUs and consumer GPUs; the base under many local-AI apps.

resources.name: LM Studio
resources.description: Polished desktop app for downloading and chatting with local models, with a local OpenAI-compatible server. Closed-source but free to download.
resources.notes: Not open source. Check LM Studio's current terms for commercial or workplace use.

resources.name: Open WebUI
resources.description: Self-hosted ChatGPT-style web interface that works with Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs, with RAG and multi-user features.
resources.notes: Uses a custom license with branding conditions; read it before redistributing. GitHub could not auto-detect a single standard license (it may be custom or multi-license); read the repo's license files.

resources.name: Jan
resources.description: Open-source desktop app that runs models offline and can also connect to remote APIs.
resources.notes: GitHub could not auto-detect a single standard license (it may be custom or multi-license); read the repo's license files.

resources.name: vLLM
resources.description: High-throughput LLM serving engine for GPUs; the standard choice when you self-host models for many users.

resources.name: Transformers (Hugging Face)
resources.description: The main Python library for loading and running open models across text, vision and audio.

resources.name: Diffusers (Hugging Face)
resources.description: Library for image and video generation models (Stable Diffusion, FLUX and others) in Python.

resources.name: ComfyUI

resources.name: LlamaIndex

resources.name: AnythingLLM

resources.name: MarkItDown

resources.name: Docling

resources.name: Gradio

resources.name: Streamlit

resources.name: marimo
resources.description: Reactive Python notebook that stores notebooks as plain .py files and can be deployed as an app.

resources.name: OpenRouter
resources.description: One API key and OpenAI-compatible endpoint for hundreds of models, including several ':free' model variants with tight rate limits.

free_tier.summary: Free model variants exist with daily/per-minute caps; adding a small credit balance raises caps (see OpenRouter's limits docs).

resources.name: Groq
resources.description: Very fast hosted inference for open models with a rate-limited free tier.

free_tier.summary: Rate-limited free tier; check the console for current per-model limits.

resources.name: Cerebras Inference
resources.description: High-speed hosted inference for open models with a free developer tier.

free_tier.summary: Free developer tier with rate limits; check the current limits page.

resources.name: Mistral La Plateforme

free_tier.summary: Free experimentation tier with rate limits; check current terms (free-tier data-use conditions may apply).

resources.name: GitHub Models

free_tier.summary: Rate-limited free access for prototyping; limits depend on the model and your GitHub plan.

resources.name: NVIDIA Build (NIM API catalog)

free_tier.summary: Free prototyping access with limits; check the terms shown on each model page.

resources.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
resources.description: Run open models (text, image, speech, embeddings) from Cloudflare Workers with a daily free allocation.

free_tier.summary: Free daily allocation, then pay-as-you-go; check the pricing page for the current amount.

resources.name: Hugging Face Inference Providers

free_tier.summary: Free accounts get a very small monthly credit (about $0.10 reported); PRO gets about $2/month; beyond that you pay provider rates.

resources.name: Cohere Trial Keys

free_tier.summary: Free monthly credits (amount has changed over time; phone verification has been reported).

resources.name: Modal

free_tier.summary: Monthly free credits on the starter plan; check current amount.

resources.name: Oracle Cloud Always Free
resources.description: Oracle's Always Free resources, best known for small Arm-based VMs that can host side projects or self-hosted apps indefinitely.

free_tier.summary: Always Free resources have fixed quotas; Arm capacity is sometimes unavailable in a region and idle instances can be reclaimed.

resources.notes: Read Oracle's Always Free terms and idle-resource policy before hosting anything important.

resources.name: Lovable
resources.description: Prompt-to-app builder that generates a React front end with backend and database wiring and lets you publish and sync to GitHub.

free_tier.summary: Free plan: 5 build credits per day, capped at 30 per month, plus small monthly Cloud/AI grants; custom domains are not included (as reported Aug 2026).

resources.name: Bolt.new
resources.description: Browser-based AI app builder that scaffolds, edits and previews full-stack JavaScript projects and can deploy them.

free_tier.summary: Free plan reported at about 1M tokens per month with a 300K daily cap; Bolt branding stays on free projects; custom domains need a paid plan (July 2026 reports).

resources.name: v0
resources.description: Vercel's AI builder for React/Tailwind/shadcn UI. Accepts prompts and images, offers a visual Design Mode, and can sync to GitHub and deploy to Vercel.

free_tier.summary: Free plan reported at $5/month of credits with a 7-messages-per-day limit (July-Aug 2026).

resources.notes: Vercel's Hobby hosting plan is limited to non-commercial use; see the hosting entries before deploying a paid product there.

resources.name: Google Stitch
resources.description: Google Labs tool that generates multi-screen UI designs from text, sketches or screenshots, can extract a design system from a URL, exports HTML/CSS, Figma paste and DESIGN.md, and offers an MCP server.

free_tier.summary: Free through Google Labs with a daily credit limit that resets at midnight UTC and no paid plan (per Google's FAQ as captured June 2026). Exact limits have changed several times.

resources.name: Replit
resources.description: Browser IDE with an AI agent that can build and host apps end to end, good for beginners who want everything in one place.

free_tier.summary: Free plan exists; Replit does not publish specific numbers for free-tier agent credits (reported).

resources.name: Google Antigravity
resources.description: Google's agent-first coding IDE; Google's own FAQ points individual Gemini CLI users to Antigravity and its CLI after June 2026.

free_tier.summary: Free tier exists but the daily agent allowance is small and has been cut since launch (third-party reports); Google says offerings may keep changing.

resources.name: Kiro
resources.description: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE that turns prompts into requirements, designs and tasks before writing code.

free_tier.summary: Reported to include a small free credit allowance; verify current plans.

resources.name: Cursor
resources.description: VS Code-based editor built around AI chat, edits and agents.

free_tier.summary: A free Hobby plan exists; Cursor describes limits only as 'limited' without published numbers (per a 2026 comparison).
